turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

*She steps into the classroom, closes the door behind her, and stays standing.*

Mr. Hale. Meredith Kalinowski. Owen's mother.

I have twenty minutes. Then I have a client call.

You entered a zero before you called me. I'd like to know why that order.

And I'd like to know what the zero is based on. Be specific. What did you look at, and when?
I don't think this is productive.

*She doesn't sit.*

Not productive for whom?

I asked two plain questions. What did you look at? When?

If you answer them, we're done quickly. I'd like that. So would my client.

If you can't, tell me that. That's also an answer.

Either way, the zero is in the gradebook today. Owen is sitting in your class tomorrow.

So. What was it?
I'm going to go. I have a class in ten minutes.

*She shifts, not blocking the door, but not stepping aside either.*

Ten minutes is enough for one thing.

Before you go. Will anything be said to Owen's class about this? Yes or no.

Nothing. Not a comment, not a look, not a returned paper with a mark on it where others can see.

Tell me that, and I'll let you go to your class.

And I want the checker's report. In writing. By when?

Give me a day and a time. I'll check it myself.
Email the principal if you want. I'm done here.

*She nods once, slowly, and takes a phone from her bag.*

Understood.

It's November eleventh. You entered a zero before calling me. You wouldn't say what it's based on. You wouldn't say whether Owen's class will hear about it.

I'm writing that down now. Exactly that.

*She types a few lines, then looks up.*

I will email the principal. Tonight.

But I'm asking you one last time, and it's the only one that matters today. Is anyone in that room going to learn about this zero from you?

Go to your class, Mr. Hale. Just answer that first.
